seo.title: Villa or Hotel | TripAgent
seo.description: When a private villa is right, and when a hotel is: space and privacy against service and an address. The honest trade, and how a staffed villa is provisioned and run.

hero.lede: Space and privacy, or service and an address. Both can be wonderful. The question is which one fits this trip, and the people you're travelling with.

intro.note: A villa gives you a house of your own. A hotel gives you a staff of dozens you never see. Two different kinds of luxury.
intro.statement: Count the people and the nights.
intro.lede: Most of the time the answer arrives on its own, once you count the party and the days. A couple, three nights, a city: that is a hotel. The concierge, the restaurant downstairs, the address. A family of eight, ten days, the sea: that is a villa. The kitchen, the pool no one queues for, the long lunches no one has to ask permission for. The hard ones sit in between. That is where we earn our keep.

cols.heading: A house of your own
items: Room to breathe: bedrooms apart, space to spread out, a garden and a pool that are yours alone.
A kitchen, so meals keep your hours: late breakfasts, children fed early, a private chef if you like.
Real privacy: no lobby, no neighbours, no one watching. The freedom to be entirely off-duty.
Better value for a group: a whole villa can cost less per head than several suites, and give far more room.

cols.heading: A staff you never see
items: Service whenever you want it: housekeeping twice a day, a concierge, room service at midnight, a problem gone with one call.
The address and the life around it: the bar, the spa, the restaurant, the people. Somewhere to be, not only to sleep.
Nothing to arrange: no provisioning, no staff to manage. You simply arrive.
Easy for short stays: a single night, a city stop, anywhere a villa makes little sense.

signature.pullHtml: A hotel looks after you. A villa lets you stop being looked after. A good one can still do both.

vrow.heading: A villa, run like a hotel.
vrow.lede: The worry with a private home is that you give up service for space. You don't have to. A staffed villa can bring a hotel's care inside your own walls.
items: Staffed to suit you: housekeeping and a cook as standard, with a butler, a driver, a nanny or a private chef wherever you want them.
Ready before you land: the fridge stocked to your list, the bar set, the first dinner waiting. The home feels lived-in from the door.
The details taken care of: transfers, a local fixer on call, tables booked and days out arranged, as a hotel concierge would.
Seen before we offer it: every home checked in person or through people we trust, so the photographs match the floor and someone real is running it.

line.text: A villa for a group, a week or more, somewhere to settle. A hotel for two, a short stay, a city. When you fall between the two, tell us the trip. We'll make the call with you.

cta.heading: Villa or hotel: we'll advise.
cta.lede: Tell us the party, the place and the days. We'll say honestly which we'd choose, and look after whichever you pick from start to finish.
